id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

child.description:
The `child` is the `to` field for both types of relations (#sourceOfTruth and #parent) tracked on this type.

The `child` is the newly created model that was created as a copy of the #sourceOfTruth model.

See example on the type documentation.

sourceOfTruth.description:
The {@link ReliabilityMlModel} that is the source of truth for the {@link #child} model. During the
{@link FaultySensor} retraining process, this model was used to create the {@link #child} model by removing
the data from [faulty sensors](SensorOperationalStatusEnum).

parent.description:
The `parent` is the model that was active and was using a faulty sensor with the {@link FaultySensor} retraining
process began. This model may not be the same as the #sourceOfTruth model if the #parent model itself was
created during a previous run of the retraining process.

The #parent relation provides a more complete view of how the models were created over multiple runs of the
retraining process.

title:
See {@link FaultySensor} for the overview of the faulty sensor retraining process.

This type denotes the relationship between {@link ReliabilityMlModel}s that were created during the faulty sensor
retraining process. This allows the application logic to track which models were automatically created and develop
a history of where retrained models come from. This is useful because when a sensor becomes operational again, the
goal is to return to the original model that was using the sensor.

Example:

Notation for example: Model 1 uses sensors A, B, C = M1 (A, B, C)

Start: M1 (A, B, C)
A becomes faulty: M2 (B, C)
D becomes faulty: No change
B becomes faulty: M3 (C)
D becomes operational: No change
A becomes operational: M4 (A, C)

In order to create M4, we need to know that M1 is the source of truth for M3.

Some example relations for the above example:
- { child: M3, sourceOfTruth: M1, parent: M2 }
- { child: M4, sourceOfTruth: M1, parent: M3 }
- ...
name: FaultySensor.RiskModelSourceOfTruthRelation
